title: Do not impose on others what you do not desire
shortSummary: The answer expresses shu as restraint in treating others, beginning from what one would not wish to bear oneself.
curatorialDescription: The passage remains in its question-and-virtue context rather than becoming an isolated slogan detached from relational ethics.
researchNote: The Wei Ling Gong context, early commentary and Tang exegesis remain to be added.

sources.title: Received editions and chapter references for the Analects
sources.locator: 颜渊第十二，第1章（“克己复礼为仁”）
sources.role: Initial basis for the Confucian passage and chapter locator

profile.modernZh: 自己不愿承受的事情，不要加在别人身上。
profile.translationEn: Do not impose on others what you do not desire for yourself.
